title: Dedicated staged rollouts (Dedicated pools) — Launch checklist
content:
Owner: Connor O'Brien (Release Engineering)
PM: Talia Benson
Eng leads: Ethan Park (control plane), Mina Haddad (routing), Logan Wright (telemetry), Chloe Martin (console backend)
SRE: Sean Gallagher / Rafael Mendes
Security: Marcus Lin / Kevin Osei

Doc purpose
- A single place to run the Dedicated staged rollouts launch as a controlled change.
- This is not a product checklist; it’s the release train checklist (flags/migrations/monitoring/enablement/rollback).

Scope
- Dedicated pools only (reserved GPU pools). Hosted API rollout system is out of scope.
- v1 = deterministic staged rollout with gates, approvals, audit logging, evaluator fail-safe hold.

Environments
- dev/staging: continuous
- prod: controlled enablement with allowlist (per-tenant + operator override)

Release phases
- Phase 0: internal dogfood on Redwood-managed Dedicated pools
- Phase 1: beta enablement (2–3 enterprise customers)
- Phase 2: GA enablement (default available for Dedicated, still permissioned)


SECTION A — Pre-flight (one-time readiness)

A1. Code + artifact readiness
[ ] All required PRs merged to release branch / deployed to staging:
    - Control-plane objects + validation rules (pr_28411)
    - Rollout CRUD APIs + versioning (pr_28435)
    - Approve/abort endpoints + event emission (pr_28462)
    - Routing stage weights determinism + guardrails (pr_28479)
    - Gate evaluator service + windowing + pause-on-missing-metrics (pr_28490)
    - Audit logging structured events (pr_28558)
    - Fail-safe: evaluator degraded => hold (pr_28572)
    - Autoscaling headroom guardrails (pr_28588)
    - Integration tests (pr_28601)
[ ] Console backend + frontend included in release (if applicable to this train)
[ ] Docs PR merged (redwood-docs/pr_1442) OR internal docs path confirmed and published

A2. Dependency confirmation
[ ] Telemetry pipeline has required metrics in prod for Dedicated pools (queue depth, utilization, timeout/5xx rate)
[ ] Policy engine supports deterministic allocation with stable hashing keys for Dedicated (tenant + pool + route)
[ ] Audit log export pipeline accepts new event types and is visible in SIEM export feed

A3. Ownership + oncall
[ ] Confirm current DRI for rollout incidents during launch window:
    - Primary DRI: SRE oncall (Sean Gallagher delegate)
    - Secondary: Platform oncall (Ethan Park delegate)
    - Routing escalation: Mina Haddad delegate
    - Security escalation (audit issues): Marcus Lin delegate
[ ] Establish launch channel + incident alias (to be created by Talia): #launch-dedicated-staged-rollouts


SECTION B — Database migrations / persistence readiness

B1. Schema migrations
[ ] Migration plan reviewed by Michael Nguyen (data model & migrations)
[ ] Migration is backward-compatible (new tables/columns only; no required reads by old code)
[ ] Dry-run migration in staging completed
[ ] Roll-forward/roll-back strategy documented (see Section H)

B2. Data retention / cleanup
[ ] Audit events retention policy confirmed with Security (default retention + export). Note: audit events are security artifacts.
[ ] Any TTL/cleanup jobs for evaluator state are enabled and safe (no accidental deletion of active rollout state)


SECTION C — Feature flags / config toggles

NOTE: We must be able to hard-disable automatic stage advancement and/or the whole feature without deleting plans.

C1. Global feature flags
[ ] Flag: dedicated_staged_rollouts_enabled (default OFF in prod)
[ ] Flag: dedicated_staged_rollouts_allowlist_enforced (default ON when enabled)
[ ] Flag: dedicated_rollout_evaluator_enabled (default OFF until evaluator health verified)
[ ] Flag: dedicated_rollout_auto_advance_enabled (default OFF for dogfood; ON for beta with strict gates)
[ ] Flag: dedicated_rollout_console_ui_enabled (optional; may be operator-only)

C2. Per-tenant / per-pool allowlist
[ ] Allowlist source-of-truth confirmed (control plane config vs. admin config service)
[ ] Allowlist supports:
    - tenant_id
    - pool_id override (if we need to scope further)
    - operator_override (break-glass)

C3. Safety defaults
[ ] Missing/late metrics behavior = HOLD (not PROCEED)
[ ] Evaluator degraded behavior = HOLD
[ ] Routing behavior for stage weights validated at 0% and 100% transitions (no traffic “gaps”)


SECTION D — Observability / dashboards / alerting

D1. Dashboards
[ ] Dedicated rollout overview dashboard published (per pool: current plan version, stage, hold reason)
[ ] Gate evaluator health dashboard published:
    - evaluator tick lag
    - query latency
    - evaluation success rate
    - missing-metrics rate (by metric type)
[ ] Stage performance panels:
    - p50/p95 latency
    - 5xx + timeouts
    - queue depth
    - GPU utilization

D2. Alerts (page vs ticket)
[ ] PAGE: evaluator lag > threshold (see gating SLO doc) AND active rollouts exist
[ ] PAGE: paused/held rollouts on tier-1 pools (customer pools with SLA) where hold reason is evaluator degraded
[ ] TICKET: repeated false-positive holds (hold rate > X over 24h)
[ ] TICKET: audit event export failures

D3. Logging / traces
[ ] Structured logs include rollout identifiers: tenant_id, pool_id, rollout_plan_id, plan_version, stage_id, gate_id
[ ] Trace sampling reviewed to avoid cardinality blow-ups (reference pr_28640 if needed)


SECTION E — Security / RBAC / audit

E1. RBAC readiness
[ ] Permissions exist and are enforced across all relevant endpoints:
    - rollout.edit
    - rollout.approve
    - rollout.abort
    - rollout.view_audit
[ ] Enterprise tenant scopes validated (no cross-tenant reads/writes)
[ ] Break-glass role documented and limited (operator override)

E2. Audit logging
[ ] Audit events emitted for:
    - rollout_plan.create
    - rollout_plan.update
    - rollout_stage.approve
    - rollout.abort
    - rollout.hold (auto)
    - rollout.rollback (auto/manual)
[ ] Audit events include: actor, actor_type, tenant_id, pool_id, plan_version, stage_id, request_id
[ ] Security has reviewed schema and retention assumptions (Marcus Lin sign-off)


SECTION F — Validation in staging (required before prod enablement)

F1. Happy path test
[ ] Create rollout plan with 3 stages (5% / 25% / 100%) + defaults gates
[ ] Approve stage 1, verify deterministic traffic allocation and routing logs
[ ] Verify stage auto-advances only when evaluator marks gates PASS for entire evaluation window
[ ] Verify can pause/abort from console and via API

F2. Failure path tests
[ ] Force gate failure (e.g., p95 latency) => rollout holds and does NOT advance
[ ] Force missing metrics => rollout holds with reason=missing_metrics
[ ] Force evaluator lag/degrade => rollout holds and auto-advance blocked
[ ] Verify rollback behavior (manual abort and “rollback to previous config/model” path) does not overload pool

F3. Performance/regression
[ ] Run load test scenario on staging reserved pool (from dedicated-rollout-load-test-plan) and confirm no unexpected queue depth spikes during stage shift
[ ] Confirm autoscaling headroom guardrail triggers appropriately (does not proceed into stage that would violate headroom)

F4. Determinism checks
[ ] Same request hashing key yields stable assignment across evaluator ticks and process restarts
[ ] No cross-tenant interference (validate isolation by tenant_id and pool_id boundaries)


SECTION G — Internal enablement (operators + SRE + Support)

G1. Training / walkthrough
[ ] 30-min operator training scheduled (DRIs: Chloe Martin + Sean Gallagher)
    Agenda:
    - Creating a rollout plan
    - What gates mean and how evaluation windows work
    - What “HOLD” states look like and how to respond
    - Approval + audit trail expectations
[ ] Oncall runbook reviewed in training: “Runbook — Dedicated staged rollout paused”

G2. Support / CS readiness
[ ] Support escalation path documented (Dev Patel + Owen Phillips)
[ ] Beta customer comms template ready (Rachel Kim)
[ ] Known limitations written down (for Support to copy/paste):
    - Feature is allowlist-only
    - Gate types limited to latency/errors/queue depth/utilization in v1
    - Missing metrics pauses rollout

G3. Documentation
[ ] Internal docs published (operator FAQ + API examples)
[ ] Console UX notes published for operator-only view
[ ] Release notes draft prepared for beta (Product: Marissa Cole)


SECTION H — Production rollout plan (step-by-step)

H0. Go/No-Go checklist (must be YES to proceed)
[ ] Staging validation complete (Section F all checked)
[ ] SRE sign-off on alerts/pages (Sean Gallagher)
[ ] Security sign-off on audit events (Marcus Lin)
[ ] Dedicated product sign-off that the allowlist set is correct (Lauren Bishop)
[ ] Rollback plan reviewed and tested in staging (H4)

H1. Prod deploy
[ ] Deploy services with flags OFF (no behavior change)
[ ] Verify no increase in error rate / latency post-deploy
[ ] Verify evaluator service is running but disabled (or running in “observe-only” mode)

H2. Enable for internal dogfood
[ ] Turn ON dedicated_staged_rollouts_enabled for internal Redwood tenant(s) only
[ ] Turn ON evaluator for internal only
[ ] Keep auto-advance OFF for first 24h; use manual approvals only
[ ] Create 1–2 rollout plans on Redwood-managed dedicated pools and observe dashboard + audit log behavior

H3. Enable for beta customers
[ ] Add beta tenants to allowlist (Rachel Kim confirms contacts + pool_ids)
[ ] Turn ON evaluator + auto-advance for beta tenants only
[ ] Confirm default gates and evaluation window are set to recommended SLOs (ref: dedicated-rollouts-gating-slos)
[ ] Schedule first customer rollout window with SRE present (or on standby)
[ ] Capture learnings + issues in Linear (link to PM-418)

H4. GA enablement
[ ] Expand allowlist to broader set of Dedicated tenants OR flip policy to allow by default (depends on GA decision)
[ ] Confirm console UI is available for intended roles only
[ ] Confirm Support is ready for increased ticket volume in first 2 weeks


SECTION I — Rollback plan (keep this short and executable)

Rollback goals
- Stop further progression (no new stage advancement)
- Prevent unsafe routing changes
- Preserve audit trail and state for later analysis

I1. Immediate “stop the line” actions (no deploy required)
[ ] Disable dedicated_rollout_auto_advance_enabled globally (or for impacted tenants)
[ ] If evaluator degraded or producing bad holds: disable dedicated_rollout_evaluator_enabled (rollouts should HOLD and not proceed)
[ ] If routing behavior is incorrect: disable dedicated_staged_rollouts_enabled (falls back to pre-rollout pool routing behavior)

I2. If data plane/pool is saturated due to rollout
[ ] Abort rollout via API/console (ensures stage weight returns to safe baseline)
[ ] If abort path is blocked, apply emergency routing override (routing oncall + SRE)
[ ] Consider temporary capacity actions for the pool (Dedicated ops: Vanessa Ortiz / Keiko Yamamoto)

I3. If DB migration caused issues
[ ] Prefer roll-forward fix (do not drop tables/columns)
[ ] If absolutely necessary, disable feature flags and keep schema in place; schedule post-incident fix

I4. Post-rollback hygiene
[ ] Open incident if customer impact occurred
[ ] Export audit events and attach to incident timeline
[ ] Create follow-up tasks (missing metrics, evaluator lag, guardrail tuning)


SECTION J — Launch comms + tracking

J1. Internal comms
[ ] Announce dogfood enablement in #eng-platform + #eng-sre with dashboard links
[ ] Announce beta enablement plan in #customer-success + #support with escalation steps

J2. External (beta customers)
[ ] Confirm change window and success criteria
[ ] Confirm who is authorized to approve/abort (customer roles vs Redwood operator)
[ ] Provide short “what to expect” summary:
    - staged weights
    - gates and evaluation window
    - what HOLD looks like
    - how to request abort

J3. KPIs to track for first 2 weeks
[ ] Number of rollouts started / completed / held
[ ] Hold reasons distribution (gate fail vs missing metrics vs evaluator degraded)
[ ] False-positive hold rate (SRE judgment)
[ ] Incidents or SLA-impacting events related to rollouts


Notes / open items
- Confirm GA posture: allowlist-only vs available-by-default-but-permissioned (Product + Security decision)
- Decide whether we want “observe-only evaluator” mode in prod for a week before enabling auto-advance
- Ensure the autoscaling headroom guardrail default is not too strict for small pools (risk: perpetual hold)
